- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days by 15–30% of recent spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model over-anticipates decline; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days by 15–30% of recent drop magnitude.
- Model consistently under-forecasts true outcomes in early horizon (1–5 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 10–20% upward bias for first 5 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply 20–40% downward correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model fails to mean-revert; apply 10–25% mean-reversion bias toward historical 10-day average for next 5–7 days.
- Model under-forecasts in high-sentiment periods when true outcomes are trending upward; increase forecast by 15–30% for 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.67 and true outcome > 1.5x recent average.
